text.p: These are the leading stories in Skopje press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.

- Only Social-Democrats supported government-proposed law on Albanian-language classes in Skopje Teachers' academy. Ethnic Albanian deputies opposed to law and demand "legalisation of Tetovo university".

- British Ambassador Tony Milson denied reports in Macedonian press that Britain and Greece blocked financial aid to Macedonia. He explained Britain wanted the financial aid to be extended to Macedonia as grant not as credit. It would be unfair to burden country in this phase of development with an additional debt, the ambassador told paper.

- The main reason for postponement of visit of Albanian Prime Minister Alleksandar Mesi to Skopje is Macedonia's refusal to sign agreement for abolishing visas between the two countries, says Albanian diplomat in Skopje.
- Macedonian President Kiro Gligorov appointed career diplomat Naste Calovski as ambassador in Macedonia's mission to the U.N. in New York.

- With its veto in EU for aid to Macedonia, Greece once more promotes itself as provincial, marginal player in EU. Greek attitude questions interim accord signed by two countries almost two years ago in the U.N., paper comments.

- Association of Serbs and Montenegrins from Macedonia told a news conference on Wednesday that Macedonian police banned entrance of Serbian priests to Macedonia to attend Saint Sava day celebrations, January 27.
- A special bank for support of Macedonian exports set up in Skopje. government plans to finance this institution from budget.
